title: Supply Chain Weather Forecast
subtitle: Five separate weather stations for verified exception files — no composite risk score.

stations.label: Origin-proof station
facts: Reuters reported a White House transshipment report estimating $19 billion to $26 billion in annual lost tariff revenue.
The same reporting said CBP is using AI tools to inspect container markings, packaging patterns and X-ray images for mismatches.
USTR and Federal Register forced-labor Section 301 signals move policy into dated entry and origin-proof records.
stations.decision: Attach supplier, routing, entry and origin evidence to exposed shipments before approval or customer promise.
stations.watch: CBP enforcement signals, USTR/Federal Register notices, broker exception logs and origin-proof gaps.

stations.label: Classification station
facts: Supply Chain Dive coverage of drone tariffs and Section 232 derivative proposals keeps product classification live.
Classification rows require HTS, product description, country treatment and approval evidence.
A tariff schedule alone does not prove treatment for a specific SKU or importer.
stations.decision: Assign one owner for HTS/product-master-data rows and hold exceptions where proof or legal approval is missing.
stations.watch: Federal Register updates, counsel-reviewed classifications and master-data change logs.

stations.label: Freight-capacity station
facts: FreightWaves, citing Descartes, said July U.S. containerized imports rose 4.5% from June to 2,508,310 TEUs.
FreightWaves/Xeneta reported Far East to U.S. rates still falling.
Reuters Rhine low-water reporting keeps inland-waterway fallback capacity on the watch board.
stations.decision: Keep volume, rate, booking, inventory and fallback-route assumptions as separate owner cards.
stations.watch: Descartes, NRF/Hackett, Xeneta/FreightWaves lane cards, port actuals and Rhine Kaub levels.

stations.label: Inventory-simulation station
facts: Reuters reported manufacturers using AI as inventory buffers shrink.
The Signal Translation package cites McKinsey survey work showing reliance on larger buffers down to 34% from 60% in 2022.
It also cites Gartner's estimate that supply-chain software spending including generative AI could reach $55 billion by 2029.
stations.decision: Treat AI or digital-twin output as an exception note with a named owner, approval and failure mode.
stations.watch: Planning-data quality, audit trails, override rules and pilot-to-rollout performance claims.

stations.label: Farm-to-fork proof station
facts: FAO's July Food Price Index rose 0.6% from June while cereals, vegetable oils and sugar rose and meat and dairy fell.

Supply Chain Dive reported Target's Proxima fresh-food digital-twin pilot improved on-shelf availability by 2.5% for 63 items and simulated a 1.2 million-square-foot receive center with about 98% accuracy.
Reuters reported Maharashtra suspended permits for 12 quick-commerce warehouses after inspections across 86 establishments.
stations.decision: Create proof files for input exposure, freshness, storage compliance, fallback routing and availability promises.
stations.watch: FAO category moves, food-safety inspections, supplier proof, storage permits and fresh-food availability pilots.

newsletterInsert.headline: Supply Chain Weather: five verified-exception stations
newsletterInsert.copy: This week's weather is not one risk score. It is five separate stations — origin proof, classification, freight capacity, inventory simulation and farm-to-fork proof. Each station needs a source, owner, proof artifact, deadline, approval and failure mode before the next decision.
